diagnostic_evidence.quote: The time signals excited at different moments can be separated under the Assumption \ref{sump}.

issues.failure_explanation: The duration and arrival interval of a received pulse depend on the projected locations and extents of both successive physical source supports. The displayed condition controls only the diameter of the preceding profile and does not control the displacement between pulses or the extent of the next profile. For example, the next domain may be arbitrarily large while the condition remains unchanged, so its received interval can overlap the preceding one. Thus Assumption \ref{sump} alone does not establish the asserted decomposition of aggregate data into the individual fields $u_j^\infty$.

failure_location.quote: The second assumption ensures that wave signals generated at different instants remain separable due to non-overlapping supports.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a genuine non-overlap condition formulated in terms of the arrival-time intervals of all successive physical supports, and prove that it permits extraction of each $u_j^\infty$; alternatively, withdraw the separation claim and explicitly assume the component data are independently given.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's extension from the single-pulse problem to recovery of several pulses from measured time-domain data is unsupported unless the component far fields $u_j^\infty$ are supplied separately.
issues.title: The stated pulse-spacing condition does not ensure separation of received wave signals
issues.why_classification: The alternative repair changes the advertised data model from aggregate measurements to already separated component data, while preserving the aggregate-data claim requires a new separation hypothesis and argument.

issues.failure_explanation: From the source's own definition, $\operatorname{supp}S_0=\overline D_0$, so $\operatorname{supp}S_0(\cdot-a(t_0))=a(t_0)+\overline D_0$, not $\overline D_0$ unless the translation vanishes or $D_0$ is redefined. The subsequent integration over $D$ and interpretation of $D$ as the physical source location therefore use incompatible meanings.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine $D:=a(t_0)+D_0$ and $S(x):=S_0(x-a(t_0))$, and consistently impose the boundedness and regularity assumptions on this translated physical support.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the support reconstructed by the factorization framework is not consistently identified with the physical support of the moving source.
issues.title: The translated source is assigned the wrong spatial support

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the operator $T_{\#}=|\real T| +|\ima T|: X\rightarrow X$ is coercive

issues.failure_explanation: Convergence in operator norm does not imply convergence, much less equality, of the nonclosed operator ranges. The proof only constructs approximating sequences, which at most gives closure relations. Moreover, under $|S|>0$ only almost everywhere, the multiplication operator can approach zero and need not be coercive, so the appendix range theorem cannot be applied to the limiting operator. No argument closes this gap.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove an exact limiting range theorem without coercivity, or restore a uniform lower bound on $|S|$ and thereby abandon the advertised almost-everywhere nonvanishing generalization.
issues.overall_effect: The Picard criterion is not shown to characterize $\operatorname{Range}(L)$ under the advertised weakened source assumption, invalidating the theoretical basis of all subsequent indicators and uniqueness claims.
issues.title: Operator-norm approximation does not prove the claimed exact range identity
issues.why_classification: The available repair either requires new operator-range theory or excludes the paper's advertised generalized source regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The test function is specified only on the finite interval $(0,K)$, so its inverse Fourier transform after zero extension is a sinc-type function, not a Dirac mass. More fundamentally, if $Lw(k)=e^{-ikb}$ on an interval, boundedness of $D$ makes both sides analytic in $k$, so equality extends to all real $k$. But $Lw$ is the Fourier transform of an integrable projected density and tends to zero as $|k|\to\infty$, whereas $|e^{-ikb}|=1$. Thus no $w\in L^2(D)$ can produce the point exponential, even when $b$ lies inside the projected support.

failure_location.quote: For any $\eta \in \R$, there holds $z \in {K}_{D,\eta}^{(\hat{x})}$ if and only if $\phi^{(\hat{x})}_{z,\eta} \in $ Range $(L)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, the point exponential must be replaced by a range-compatible spatially averaged test function or the criterion must be reformulated using closure or regularized approximate range membership, followed by a new indicator analysis.
issues.overall_effect: The exact pointwise range characterization is false, so the proposed point-defined indicator functions do not have the asserted zero-versus-positive support behavior and the resulting uniqueness claims are unproved.
issues.title: A point exponential cannot belong to the range of the volume data-to-pattern operator
issues.why_classification: Repair requires abandoning the central exact pointwise range criterion and replacing the proof and indicator architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The last equality follows from the choice of $\{y_m\} ^{\infty}_{m=1}$ and the fact that $S\in C(\overline{D})$.

issues.failure_explanation: For a three-dimensional domain of positive volume, $N$ balls of radius $|D|/N$ have total volume of order $N(|D|/N)^3=O(N^{-2})$, so they cannot cover $D$ for all large $N$. Even apart from this impossibility, a covering condition does not make the equally weighted samples a valid Riemann quadrature, and operator convergence would not imply equality of exact ranges. Hence the asserted finite-dimensional range limit has no valid construction or proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, construct a valid volume quadrature and prove an appropriate operator convergence theorem, then replace the unjustified equality of exact ranges by a rigorously established relation strong enough for the intended membership conclusion.
issues.overall_effect: The finite-dimensional approximation argument used to put point exponentials into $\operatorname{Range}(L)$ fails independently of the intrinsic failure of the point-test theorem.
issues.title: The discretizing point sequence cannot satisfy the stated covering property
issues.why_classification: The stated construction is impossible, and correcting quadrature convergence alone would still require new nontrivial range-convergence theory.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $F^{(\hat x)}$ is a $N\times N$ complex matrix.

issues.failure_explanation: For a general complex matrix, its eigenvectors need not diagonalize its self-adjoint real and imaginary parts, and therefore need not diagonalize $|\operatorname{Re}F|+|\operatorname{Im}F|$. The Toeplitz construction is not shown to have the simultaneous diagonalizability needed for the claimed deduction, so the eigenvalues and vectors inserted into the indicators may be wrong.

failure_location.quote: Denoting by  $\left\{ ( {\tilde \lambda^{( x)}_n}, \psi^{(x)}_n): n=1,2,\cdots,N \right\}$ an eigen-system of the matrix $F^{(\hat x)}$ (\ref{matF}), then one deduces that  an eigen-system of the matrix $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#:= |\real (F^{(\hat x)})|+|\ima(F^{(\hat x)})|$ is $\left\{ ( \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n, \psi^{(\hat x)}_n): n=1,2,\cdots,N \right\}$, where $ \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n:=|\real (\tilde \lambda^{(\hat x)}_n)| +|\ima (\tilde \lambda^{( \hat x)}_n)|$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Form the discrete matrix $(F^{(\hat x)})_\#$ directly and compute its own spectral decomposition, as suggested by the source's alternative SPD implementation.
issues.overall_effect: The stated numerical implementation can evaluate all discrete Picard indicators using an incorrect eigensystem.
issues.title: Eigenpairs of the complex far-field matrix do not determine eigenpairs of its sharp part
issues.why_classification: Directly diagonalizing the constructed positive matrix is a short local replacement that preserves the intended numerical indicators and data requirements.
